lenses.lens: LENS 1 — science / claims / efficacy (cognitive-science-principles §3, §4, §5, §6). Adversarial, read-only, HEAD 8a06b9ac.
lenses.verdict: PASS_WITH_LIMITATIONS — R3 claims discipline HOLDS (anti-capacity rule in code, far-transfer lexicon covers focus2, live copy neutral, transfer=HYPOTHESIS in docs). No P0/P1 from this lens; the core R2 falsification is sound and not disputed. Ceiling = R3 CANDIDATA. Four forward (design-level) science gaps found, most-severe first, all P2/P3 because focus2 is CONTRACT_INERT and nothing launches.

findings.title: Reliability paradox (Hedge 2018) applied only to retire DELTA scores; retained descriptive d' (S_full) is itself a low-reliability metric and the ADR's forward reliable-change/contrast design is built ON d' with no reliability/SEM/test-retest gate; Kucina 2023 uncited
findings.epistemic_class: STATICALLY_VERIFIED (citation scope + design intent); INFERENCE (forward harm projection). NOT_RUN — no build/harness executed.
findings.evidence: EXERCISE_PORTFOLIO_V5.md:9 retires 'RT_DELTA, ACCURACY_DELTA, PRESSURE_DELTA, SSRT ... (E013 Hedge: paradoja de fiabilidad)' but does NOT list d'. ADR_FOCUS_TEMPORAL_QUALITY.md:846 '(b) ... reliable-change/contraste se computan de S_full por condición' and :74/§R3-5:152-153 keep d' as the retained descriptive value with only an MNAR aggregation caveat. DescriptiveScorer.kt computes d' per condition (loglinear) but grep of focus2/**.kt for 'reliab|SEM|test-retest|reliable.?change|Hedge|split.?half' = 0 hits — no reliability handling in code. Repo grep 'Kucina' = 0 hits. Tracers are exactly Hedge's low-reliability tasks: FOC2-E07 is a flanker/filtering task, FOC2-E01 a detection/vigilance task.
findings.failure_mode: Hedge/Kucina show conflict- and detection-type contrasts (flanker, Stroop, SSRT, and SDT d') have poor between-subject test-retest reliability because within-subject variance dwarfs between-subject variance — so a per-condition d' is a weak individual-differences instrument. The docs caught this for the DELTA scores yet keep d' AND plan cross-session 'reliable-change' on it. When S6+ unlocks longitudinal comparison, a reliable-change claim on a metric with unquantified (likely low) reliability would present practice effects, regression-to-the-mean, and measurement noise as genuine capacity change — the precise false-progress the doctrine (§4) forbids, and a violation of §5 (report reliability + SEM, not point scores).
findings.fix_now: Register that S_full=d' inherits the reliability paradox the docs already cite for deltas; forbid any cross-session reliable-change/contrast on S_full until a between-subject test-retest reliability coefficient (and SEM) is measured for each tracer; add Kucina 2023 alongside Hedge 2018 as authority for d'/RT-conflict reliability, not only for the retired deltas.
findings.definitive_fix: Make measured per-tracer reliability (ICC/test-retest + SEM) an explicit V-gate blocker that must PASS before any longitudinal d' comparison or 'reliable-change' is computed or shown; encode a reliable-change formula that uses the measured SEM.
findings.closing_test: A doc/gate asserting no cross-session contrast on S_full is derivable without a measured reliability coefficient; a psychometric report giving test-retest ICC + SEM per tracer before reliable-change is enabled.
findings.residual_risk: Even with reliability measured, near-transfer d' change on the trained task is not capacity transfer (training-to-the-test); V3+ validity gates remain independent prerequisites.

findings.title: Target population and minors are UNDEFINED for the product, and the only doc that acknowledges this is unresolved is explicitly EXCLUDED from the external audit package
findings.epistemic_class: STATICALLY_VERIFIED (doc reads). NOT_VERIFIABLE — PRD itself not read (outside focus_v5); relied on the reviewed-plan's characterization.
findings.evidence: FOCUS_ENGINE_MASTER_PLAN_V5.md:378 recruitment is 'adultos — LCH-003'; :568 R-15 registers 'Alpha con menores o consentimiento inválido' as a RISK (participant <18) gated to V2 — both are ALPHA-research scope, not the shipped product. S5_R4_PASO7_PLAN_REVIEWED.md:446 row1 'Intended use / población objetivo exacta | parcial (PRD) | ... NO | ... CEO+producto' and :457/:460 rows 12/15 mark DPIA/minors and user-risk (minors) as NO/parcial. That reviewed-plan doc is on the EXCLUDE list of the external package: S5_R3_P7_HANDOFF.md:97-100 excludes 'S5_R4_PASO7_PLAN_REVIEWED.md ...' from the audit bundle (host-path hygiene). No age-gate/target-population definition exists in the INCLUDED R3 artifacts (evidence capsule / handoff / authority index).
findings.failure_mode: A cognitive-training product with efficacy still at DESIGNED_NOT_RUN, whose north-star is 'the average user' (§6), cannot claim or calibrate efficacy for a population it has not defined — cognitive norms and RT/d' distributions are strongly age-dependent, and minors carry GDPR-K/COPPA weight and a distinct efficacy-claims risk. Because the acknowledgment that this is unresolved sits only in an excluded process doc, the external auditor sees no signal that population/minors is an open blocker — an audit blind-spot on a science/ethics precondition.
findings.fix_now: Surface 'target population + minors handling = UNDEFINED / BLOCKER (owner CEO+product; privacy+DPO)' as an explicit line inside an INCLUDED audit artifact (handoff §4 blockers or the evidence capsule), not only in the excluded reviewed-plan.
findings.definitive_fix: Define the product target population and an age-gate/minors policy before any S6 human exposure; make it a named precondition of mount alongside W1–W5.
findings.closing_test: The external package contains an explicit population/minors BLOCKER row; mount gate checklist includes an age-gate decision.
findings.residual_risk: Population definition is a product/legal call the model cannot conclude; DPIA determination is deferred to DPO.

findings.title: Paso-7 DoD ticks 'PROVISIONAL not used for unvalidated data' while the shipped policy emits PROVISIONAL precisely for shadow/unvalidated sessions, and the ADR's own R3-11 requirement to disambiguate the ceiling name was not resolved (doc-only handoff)
findings.evidence: FocusEvidenceStatePolicy.kt:47 'else -> FocusEvidenceState.PROVISIONAL' is the ceiling returned for a clean, dose-complete (unvalidated, shadow) session; KDoc :26 'PROVISIONAL is the ceiling'. ADR §R3-11 (ADR_FOCUS_TEMPORAL_QUALITY.md:277-281) says PROVISIONAL 'SÍ insinúa perfil' in the sibling cognitive lane and 'Paso 7 debe fijar un nombre inequívoco'. Yet the DoD §R3-22 (:495) ticks 'PROVISIONAL no se usa para datos no validados ✓', and the Paso-7 handoff is doc-only ('NO toca código', S5_R3_P7_HANDOFF.md:6,11) — so the name was NOT fixed and the tick is unsupported by the code.
findings.failure_mode: A single ambiguous state name shared with a lane where PROVISIONAL insinuates profile/measurement eligibility is a claims-leak: if PROVISIONAL surfaces in S6 UX it reads as a 'provisional score/measurement', implying an efficacy claim the system explicitly cannot make (OFFICIAL_ELIGIBLE is inconstructible by design). The self-checkmark makes the DoD look satisfied when it is not.
findings.fix_now: Either rename the focus2 ceiling to an unambiguous training-only token, or bind it to copy that negates measurement, and correct the DoD tick to PENDING until then.
findings.definitive_fix: Resolve the ceiling name in the real S5 close (ADR versioning), with a name-parity test that forbids reading the focus2 ceiling as measurement.
findings.owning_phase: S5 close / S6 copy mount; efficacy + product-ux
findings.closing_test: Test asserting the focus2 ceiling state name cannot be rendered as a score/measurement; DoD line reflects code reality.
findings.residual_risk: Low while unmounted; escalates the moment S6 wires a results/feedback surface.

findings.title: The 'no capacity claim / no subscore' half of the C0 semantic ceiling has NO mechanical enforcement — the copy scanner blocks far-transfer/clinical/pseudoscience lexemes but not same-construct capacity verbs or a rendered subscore
findings.epistemic_class: STATICALLY_VERIFIED (lexicon content + scanner scope + live copy). No live breach today.
findings.evidence: ForbiddenLexicon.kt:38-71 gates far-transfer/clinical/gambling/misinformation/pseudoscience, but nothing gates same-construct capacity phrasing ('entrena tu atención sostenida', 'mejora tu concentración', 'tu capacidad de enfoque') — 'atención'/'enfoque'/'capacidad'/'sostenida' are permitted words. C0 per EXERCISE_PORTFOLIO_V5.md:5-6 additionally requires 'Ningún ejercicio muestra subscore en C0; feedback descriptivo por-tarea'. Scanner covers focus2 (build.gradle.kts:443-447) so far-transfer copy is blocked, but the no-subscore / no-capacity-verb rule is enforced only by human design review. Current live copy (FocusTracerScreen.kt:110-243) is clean — forward gap only.
findings.failure_mode: When S6 wires the session results/feedback screen (which does not exist yet), a capacity claim ('mejora tu atención sostenida') or a visible per-task subscore would pass the mechanical gate, silently breaching the C0 ceiling that is the product's core anti-inflation control — exactly the failure the doctrine (§3 near vs far, §6 no misinformation) is built to prevent.
findings.fix_now: Add the 'no rendered subscore in C0' and 'no same-construct capacity verb' checks to the S6 mount acceptance (scanner rule for capacity verbs adjacent to the construct name, plus a UI check that no scalar subscore is rendered), not only the far-transfer lexicon.
findings.definitive_fix: Extend mindboostCopySafetyScanner (or a focus2-specific gate) with construct-capacity phrase patterns and a UI test asserting no subscore composable renders while state<OFFICIAL_ELIGIBLE.
findings.closing_test: A gate/test that fails if a capacity verb near 'atención/enfoque' or a numeric subscore appears in focus2 feedback copy/UI while C0.
findings.residual_risk: Semantic capacity claims are open-ended; a lexeme scanner cannot catch every paraphrase — human efficacy review of any new focus2 copy remains required.

lenses.lens: LENS 2 — psychometrics / statistics / missingness (§3.2, §3.3): the R3 eligibility estimand, its input denylist, coverage-monotonicity, and — the core charge — whether the missingness induced by technical exclusion (excludedFraction) is MNAR and whether the R3 contract addresses it.
lenses.verdict: FAIL-to-freeze on missingness grounds (ceiling: R3 CANDIDATA cannot be certified psychometrically complete). The R2 falsification is real and the R3 shape is genuinely outcome-independent (both good), but (a) one shipped file collapses an underivable excludedFraction to 0.0 in the exact direction its sibling calls fail-closed, inverting exclusion selection by device tier; (b) the R3 contract (D-R3-01..04) defines NO session-level missingness/MNAR policy for the eligibility gate — outcome-independence is conflated with ignorable missingness; (c) R3 silently dropped R2's differential-exclusion (within-session MNAR) detector, leaving its threshold an orphan. All defects are contained by CONTRACT_INERT_NO_WIRING (unmounted), so residual is capped at "biases any FUTURE measurement", not a live breach.

findings.title: Underivable excludedFraction is fail-OPEN (→0.0, no backstop, PROVISIONAL) in FocusEvidenceStatePolicy but fail-CLOSED (→1.0, SESSION_BACKSTOP_EXCEEDED) in FocusTemporalEligibility — device-tier MNAR bypass of the exclusion backstop
findings.evidence: FocusEvidenceStatePolicy.kt:45 `(temporal?.excludedFraction ?: NO_BACKSTOP) > thresholds.sessionExcludedMax` with :60 `NO_BACKSTOP: Double = 0.0`; contrast FocusTemporalEligibility.kt:87 `(excludedFraction ?: FULLY_EXCLUDED) > thresholds.sessionExcludedMax` with :101 `FULLY_EXCLUDED = 1.0`. Same null quantity, opposite fail direction. FocusTemporalEligibility KDoc:17-20 explicitly forbids reading absent temporal cells as a fabricated extreme ('reading empty cells as 0 bad windows would fabricate a maximum ... Absence is its own typed state').
findings.failure_mode: A session with no temporal capture (probe-less platform, older API, iOS-unwired, or windows-classified=0) yields excludedFraction=null. The accuracy-evidence ceiling maps null→0.0→ '0% excluded' → the session ESCAPES the exclusion backstop and reaches PROVISIONAL. Because temporal-capture availability correlates with device tier (authoritative FrameMetrics is newer-Android only), the backstop bites only well-instrumented (typically higher-end) devices while the devices most likely to have real temporal degradation escape it. The quality filter's applicability is correlated with the very characteristic that predicts the quality problem — a textbook MNAR-inducing gate that inverts the intended selection. Violates charter null≠0 and the module's own NotCaptured design rule.
findings.fix_now: In evidenceOf, do not coerce null to 0.0. A null (underivable) excludedFraction on a session that DID declare temporal capability must be treated as NotCaptured on the temporal axis, not as zero-exclusion; the accuracy lane may still be PROVISIONAL but the decision must be routed through the typed NotCaptured state, and the two consumers must share ONE constant for 'absence' (not FULLY_EXCLUDED=1.0 here and NO_BACKSTOP=0.0 there).
findings.definitive_fix: Make excludedFraction a typed three-state (Derivable(x) | Underivable | NotCaptured) so no consumer can pick a fail direction by choosing a sentinel; unify the backstop decision behind one function that both the RT lane and the accuracy lane call. Owning phase: F-R3-G / F-R3-E (psychometrician + cognitive-engine-dev), before any S6 mount.
findings.closing_test: Property test: a session with probeCapability present but zero classified windows (excludedFraction underivable) must NOT reach PROVISIONAL via a 0.0 backstop; and a probe-less session's evidence state must be derived from an explicit NotCaptured branch, not from excludedFraction=0.0. Mutation: flipping NO_BACKSTOP to 1.0 must change at least one asserted outcome (proving the constant is load-bearing and tested).
findings.residual_risk: Unmounted today (CONTRACT_INERT), so no live mis-attribution; risk is that S6 wires this as-is and the device-tier selection becomes invisible in cohort/baseline statistics.

findings.title: R3 contract (D-R3-01..04) defines NO session-level missingness/MNAR policy for the eligibility gate; outcome-independence is treated as if it were ignorable missingness
findings.evidence: ADR §R3-5 (D-R3-01), §R3-11 (D-R3-02): the ONLY MNAR treatment in the R3 candidate is the within-session behavioral survivorship of the scorer's CI_lower/DEGENERATE invalidation ('prohibido agregarlos sobre supervivientes ... sesgo MNAR al alza +0.17..0.24 d′', line 285). Grep of the ADR for MNAR/missing/selection in the R3 range (34-507) returns only §R3-11 + the lens summary. The harness self-note (r2_falsification_harness.mjs:359-361) explicitly disclaims: 'Does NOT prove ... that excludedFraction itself is free of MNAR (a separate empirical question, see report)' — and no report resolves it. §R3-17 flags inputModality/screenReaderActive as assistive-tech proxies but never connects them to exclusion selection.
findings.failure_mode: The eligibility gate excludes a session when excludedFraction > sessionExcludedMax. excludedFraction is driven by EXCLUDED-bucket windows (device jank/TRUNCATION_RISK/BUFFER_OVERFLOW), PAUSE_DISCARD (fatigue, interruption, caregiving, disability), and CLOCK_EPOCH (backgrounding). None are random w.r.t. person/device/context. The surviving 'eligible' pool is therefore a non-random sample; when S6 aggregates descriptive statistics or computes 'vs your own baseline', low-end-device / high-interruption / disability-correlated users are systematically underrepresented, and the bias is invisible because eligibility is presented as a neutral quality gate. Outcome-independence (D-R3-01) removes the mg-1 non-monotonicity but does nothing for this between-session selection.
findings.fix_now: Add a D-R3-05 that names the missingness estimand for the eligibility selection: state the ignorability assumption being made, forbid naive pooling of descriptive statistics over exclusion-survivors without a sensitivity analysis (mirror the §R3-11 'no naive aggregation over survivors' rule but for temporal exclusion, not just CI_lower), and require excludedFraction and its by-reason breakdown to be carried to any aggregation as a covariate.
findings.definitive_fix: Preregister a missingness analysis for S6: retain excludedFraction + reason mix + device/modality/screenReader stratifiers per eligible session; run a selection-model / inverse-probability-weighting sensitivity check before any cohort or baseline claim. Owning phase: assessment-psychometrics + CEO (F-R3-K physical/empirical gate).
findings.closing_test: Documentation gate: a D-R3-0x that (1) names the estimand and unit, (2) states the exclusion-missingness assumption, (3) bans unweighted aggregation over survivors, (4) requires stratifier retention. Plus a data test that the eligible-session record actually carries excludedFraction + reason mix for downstream weighting.
findings.residual_risk: Even with a policy, the true missingness mechanism is empirical and cannot be verified until S6 device-matrix + physical validation; the estimate carries the same 'UNKNOWN causal validity' ceiling the ADR already assigns to D_real.

findings.title: R3 dropped R2's differential-exclusion (within-session MNAR) detector; differentialExclusionDelta=0.15 is now an orphan constant with zero consumers and no R3 follow-up
findings.evidence: Grep `differentialExclusionDelta` across shared/src returns ONLY the declaration TemporalQualityThresholds.kt:25 (no consumer). The detector it parameterizes lives only in the R2 HISTORY (ADR §10.1, lines 815-824: 'max − min de excludedFraction por condición > differentialExclusionDelta ⇒ Absent(DIFFERENTIAL_TEMPORAL_EXCLUSION)'). The R3 candidate's follow-ups (§R3-16 F-R3-A..L) and frozen tests (§R3-20) contain NO differential-exclusion item; §R3-14 does not list DIFFERENTIAL as a value the snapshot must persist.
findings.failure_mode: Differential technical exclusion — jank/pause/epoch loss falling asymmetrically on SIGNAL vs NOISE windows — biases d' directly by shrinking H and F unequally (excluding signal windows lowers hits, raising or lowering d' depending on which cell loses more). This is outcome-INDEPENDENT to detect (it reads per-condition excludedFraction, a τ fact, fully compatible with D-R3-01), yet R3's rewrite retired the mg-1 gate AND, as collateral, the legitimate differential detector, leaving condition-asymmetric exclusion unguarded on BOTH the eligibility lane and the descriptive-value lane. The constant that would parameterize the guard is dead code.
findings.fix_now: Either (a) reinstate the differential-exclusion check as a τ-based value-lane guard in R3's follow-up list (per-condition excludedFraction spread > differentialExclusionDelta ⇒ descriptive value Absent(DIFFERENTIAL_TEMPORAL_EXCLUSION)), or (b) if intentionally deferred, delete differentialExclusionDelta and document the deferral so no orphan magic number implies a control that does not exist.
findings.definitive_fix: Implement the differential detector with the constant wired, add its property test, and record DIFFERENTIAL as a persisted reason so it survives to aggregation. Owning phase: cognitive-engine-dev + psychometrician.
findings.owning_phase: S5 R3 remediation / new follow-up (differential exclusion)
findings.closing_test: Adversarial fixture: a session where all excluded windows land on the signal condition (max−min excludedFraction across conditions > delta) must yield Absent(DIFFERENTIAL_TEMPORAL_EXCLUSION) on the descriptive value; a balanced-exclusion session must not. Mutation: setting differentialExclusionDelta absurdly high must turn the adversarial test red (proving the constant is consumed).
findings.residual_risk: Detector only catches BETWEEN-condition asymmetry; WITHIN-condition MNAR (e.g., harder trials excluded more) still needs the F-L2-02 policy.

findings.title: Harness proves R3 monotonicity/non-interference for a 1-line toy (ceiling 0.20), not the shipped FocusTemporalEligibility.evaluate (ceiling 0.50, three interacting causes); the property test that would cover the real function is NOT_RUN
findings.evidence: Harness r3Eligibility is a 4-line function over a single input with SESSION_EXCLUDED_MAX=0.20 (r2_falsification_harness.mjs:191-195), whereas the shipped default is 0.50 (TemporalQualityThresholds.kt:43) and the real evaluate has three isotone causes — NON_AUTHORITATIVE_CLASS, COVERAGE_INCOMPLETE, SESSION_BACKSTOP_EXCEEDED (FocusTemporalEligibility.kt:84-90). Harness note (:359-361) admits 'Contract-level only ... Does NOT prove the code is wired'. The real property/mutation tests (M1 monotone, M-OI outcome-independence) are PENDING per ADR §R3-5 ('conforme-pero-sin-sellar ... PENDIENTE (F-R3-G) congelar la propiedad con el property test + la mutación M-OI') and §R3-16 F-R3-G.
findings.failure_mode: Monotonicity and outcome-independence of the SHIPPED evaluate rest on the §R3-1 Lemma-2 hand argument (adders are isotone), not on an executed test. The harness's PASS certifies a toy that shares neither the threshold nor the cause structure with production, so a capsule reader could over-read 'R3 SHAPE monotone' as covering the real function. Any future edit that makes a cause non-isotone (e.g., a floor added to E over admissible counts, which §R3-5 forward-guard (1) warns about) would reintroduce outcome-dependence undetected until F-R3-G is written.
findings.fix_now: Label the R3 monotonicity/non-interference claim as INFERENCE (argued, not verified for the shipped function) wherever the capsule/handoff presents it; do not let the harness PASS stand in for the shipped-code property.
findings.definitive_fix: Write M1 + M-OI as desktopTest against the real FocusTemporalEligibility.evaluate with the straddle fixture (excludedFraction == sessionExcludedMax boundary) so the mutation cannot pass vacuously (per §R3-20 anti-vacuity). Owning phase: psychometrician + test-engineer, F-R3-G.
findings.closing_test: M-OI: reintroducing any outcome-derived term (CI_lower / S_adm) into E turns ≥1 test red, with the base fixture straddling the ceiling; M1: every degradation sequence leaves E non-improving on the real evaluate, not a toy.
findings.residual_risk: Until run, the strongest defensible claim for the shipped gate is 'argued isotone', not 'proven'.

findings.title: sessionExcludedMax=0.50 admits ~49%-compromised sessions as Eligible/PROVISIONAL and the descriptive value scores over ALL windows; the cutpoint is DESIGNED_NOT_RUN and its version is not persisted per session (no preregistered minimum, no missingness provenance)
findings.evidence: TemporalQualityThresholds.kt:43 SESSION_EXCLUDED_MAX=0.50 (KDoc: 'DESIGNED_NOT_RUN; ... changing any value requires a new version'). FocusTemporalEligibility.kt:81-88 computes excludedFraction over the full delivered denominator; DescriptiveScorer.scoreCells (DescriptiveScorer.kt:67-78) scores full cells and never receives excludedFraction, so eligibility and value are decoupled (ADR §R3-3/§R3-4: S_full counts truncation-risk windows). thresholdsVersion is absent from FocusRuntimeSnapshot (FocusRuntimeModel.kt:111-136 has no such field) and ADR §R3-14 lists it as 'ausente del snapshot'; grep confirms 0 hits in shared/src.
findings.failure_mode: A session can lose up to ~49% of delivered windows to technical compromise and still be 'Eligible', while the emitted d′ is computed over that compromised half — the D_real bias the ADR itself marks VALIDATION_STATUS=UNKNOWN. Worse for provenance: the cutpoint that governs missingness is (a) an unvalidated magic number frozen before any confirmatory evidence and (b) not stamped into the per-session record, so a later re-analysis cannot know which threshold excluded which session — defeating the charter §5 'preregistered minimums' and any retroactive audit. The two lanes never join, so 'Eligible' does not mean 'value computed on clean data'.
findings.fix_now: Persist thresholdsVersion (and temporalQualityModelVersion) into the snapshot in the same change that any real session is sealed, and mark the 0.50 ceiling explicitly PROVISIONAL/unvalidated wherever it is quoted; do not present an Eligible verdict as 'clean measurement'.
findings.definitive_fix: Either (a) compute the descriptive value over CLEAN windows with its own n-floor and carry excludedFraction as a mandatory caveat, or (b) tighten the ceiling under physical validation (F-R3-K) and version-stamp every classified session. Owning phase: kmp-architect (F-R3-F versions) + assessment (F-R3-K ceiling).
findings.closing_test: Golden wire-format test pinning thresholdsVersion in the sealed snapshot (a rename/omission turns it red); and a test that a 49%-excluded session is either demoted or carries excludedFraction as a non-optional caveat alongside its value.
findings.residual_risk: The 'right' ceiling is empirical; until F-R3-K it stays a placeholder, so even a persisted version only makes the arbitrariness auditable, not correct.

findings.title: FocusTemporalEligibility's COVERAGE_INCOMPLETE cause checks an internal identity (Σcells == resolvedTrials), not dose vs plannedTrials, so early-quit (dropout MNAR) cannot trigger it; the ADR's 'PROVISIONAL = clean + full-dose' claim leans on an unbound doseComplete input
findings.evidence: FocusTemporalEligibility.kt:83 `coverageComplete = windowsClassified == snapshot.resolvedTrials`, where windowsClassified = Σ temporalCells.totalTrials and resolvedTrials = Σ official tallies.totalTrials (FocusRuntimeModel.kt:142) — both count only RESOLVED trials, so this is a temporal-classification self-consistency identity, not coverage against plannedTrials (PresentTrial carries plannedTrials, FocusRuntimeModel.kt:229, but the eligibility path never reads it). Dose is enforced separately by FocusEvidenceStatePolicy.kt:44 `!doseComplete -> TRAINING_ONLY`, but doseComplete is a caller-supplied Boolean with no production producer (unmounted) and no property tying it to plannedTrials. ADR §R3-11 asserts the ceiling is for 'sesión LIMPIA + dosis-completa'.
findings.failure_mode: A user who quits at trial 5 of 40 (fatigue/dropout — itself MNAR w.r.t. ability/state) delivers 5 cleanly-classified trials; E returns coverageComplete=true and (if under the backstop) Eligible, so a cause literally named COVERAGE_INCOMPLETE can essentially never fire for the trial-loss-vs-plan meaning its name implies. The 'full-dose' precondition of the PROVISIONAL ceiling is an unbound external boolean, not derived from the sealed plan — the exact 'forgeable pre-computed eligibility flag' pattern the descriptor's lineageComplete comment (FocusSessionDescriptor.kt:119-124) was built to avoid.
findings.fix_now: Rename the cause or bind coverage to plannedTrials: compute coverage as resolvedTrials/plannedTrials (from the sealed spec.totalTrials) so COVERAGE_INCOMPLETE measures dose loss; and derive doseComplete from the plan rather than accepting it as an input.
findings.definitive_fix: Fold dose completeness into τ (derived from the sealed plannedTrials) so it is not a caller-forgeable boolean, and treat early-termination as a first-class missingness reason feeding F-L2-02's policy. Owning phase: cognitive-engine-dev.
findings.closing_test: A session with resolvedTrials < plannedTrials must set COVERAGE_INCOMPLETE (or route to TRAINING_ONLY) even when every resolved trial is cleanly classified; a full-plan clean session must not.
findings.residual_risk: The scorer's per-cell n≥20 floor (DescriptiveScorer.kt:169) already Absents tiny sessions on the VALUE axis, so no false score ships today; the defect is contract-honesty + the dropout-MNAR blind spot in E, latent until mount.

findings.title: VRR/LTPO Hz-detection methodology is not just 'partial' (as ADR already discloses) but asymmetrically weaker on Android than iOS — the platform doing the authoritative T1 work trusts a coarser, mode-level system API instead of iOS's empirically self-detected per-window median
findings.epistemic_class: STATICALLY_VERIFIED (code) / INFERENCE (real-device VRR behavior, no device available)
findings.evidence: WindowedTemporalProbe.android.kt:96-104 (rememberWindowedTemporalProbe) reads view.display?.refreshRate — a system-reported, mode-level API — once per drainWindow() call. WindowedTemporalProbe.ios.kt:91-97 (detectedHz) instead derives Hz from the MEDIAN of the ACTUAL inter-frame deltas sampled within that same window — self-detected from measured data, not trusted from a system property. The repo's own review (docs/engines/focus_v5/agent_outputs/05_mobile_performance.md:25-26, C.1 note lines 41-43) already names the specific failure mode: 'VRR/LTPO cambia el período nominal mid-sesión (baja a 10-24 Hz en estático)... en VRR re-derivar por ventana o clasificar el segmento como no-frame-locked' — i.e. the review's OWN recommended fix is exactly iOS's technique, not Android's. git diff of FrameTimingProbe.android.kt (REDTEAM #19, this session's working tree) confirms the Android fix only added per-drain system-API querying, not per-window empirical re-derivation.
findings.failure_mode: On an LTPO/content-adaptive Android panel that keeps Display.getRefreshRate() reporting its mode cap (e.g. 120) while actually pacing a static ISI segment much slower (10-24 Hz per the review), FrameStatsCalculator would classify every genuinely-normal low-rate frame as a 'drop' relative to the wrong nominal — spurious TRUNCATION_RISK/DegradedUsable verdicts on Android specifically, undermining the very physical-validation phase (Paso 6) whose job is to distinguish real jank from measurement artifact.
findings.fix_now: None (already labelled as a partial/open risk in ADR §11 line ~1057; this finding sharpens WHICH of the two known techniques is missing on Android, not that a risk exists).
findings.definitive_fix: Port iOS's median-inter-frame-delta self-detection to Android's refreshHzProvider (or run both and reconcile), so both platforms derive nominal Hz from the SAME class of evidence before Paso 6 physical validation runs. Owning phase: S5 task 0 follow-up / pre-Paso-6.
findings.closing_test: Synthetic-frame-stream test (desktopTest, already the pattern used for REDTEAM #19) that feeds Android's calculator a stream whose true pacing is 60 Hz while a fake refreshHzProvider reports 120 Hz, asserting the CURRENT code misclassifies it (documenting the gap) — then, once fixed, asserting the corrected code classifies it as clean by deriving Hz from the stream itself, matching iOS's approach.
findings.residual_risk: Cannot be verified against a real LTPO panel from this host (Windows, no device) — this finding is about methodological asymmetry in the code, not a measured on-device failure rate.

findings.title: MB-FOCUS-0035 (single-instance-per-user) is declared-not-enforced, and violating it silently corrupts the write-ahead safety net without the runtime ever noticing — evidenceAdmissible can stay true after its own crash-recovery copy was destroyed
findings.evidence: shared/src/commonMain/.../focus2/presentation/FocusTracerStateHolder.kt:148-166 (`start()`'s KDoc self-documents: 'PRECONDITION, declared and not yet enforced (MB-FOCUS-0035): at most one holder is alive per user per process... a concurrent start() would delete a sibling's in-flight buffer. This is safe only because the tracer is not mounted'). Trace: holder A calls start() -> store.sealDescriptor -> writeAheadSealed=true. Holder B (same userId, e.g. double-nav / two composables) calls start() -> scanSessionIds finds A's sessionId -> store.discard(userId, A.sessionId) deletes A's descriptor+snapshot keys from mindboost_focus2 (SecureFocusSessionStore.kt:81-85). Holder A's in-memory `runtime.snapshot` (FocusSessionRuntime.kt:73) is untouched by this — A keeps running and keeps calling checkpoint() (FocusTracerStateHolder.kt:288-294), which does a blind `store.put()` (SecureFocusSessionStore.kt:106-114) that unconditionally re-writes a NEW snapshot key with no paired descriptor (A never re-seals). checkpoint() therefore returns Stored (not Failed), so `checkpointLost` (line 292) is never set and `writeAheadSealed` (line 71, set once at A's own successful seal) is never re-evaluated against the store's current state -> `evidenceAdmissible` (lines 97-100) reads TRUE throughout, even though A's crash-recovery copy on disk no longer exists.
findings.failure_mode: If the process is killed at ANY point after B's discard and before A's complete(), A's entire in-progress measurement session is unrecoverable (FocusSessionRestore.kt would see DESCRIPTOR_ABSENT on the orphaned snapshot key and reject it) — exactly the scenario write-ahead exists to prevent — yet nothing in A's own state (`evidenceAdmissible`) ever reflected that its safety net had silently vanished. This is precisely the failure class the repo's own charter forbids: 'a write-ahead whose failure is swallowed reports a session as recoverable when nothing was recorded' (learning 2026-07-14, cited verbatim in this same file's class KDoc at line 27-28) — reproduced here via a concurrency vector the code explicitly flags as unenforced rather than via a swallowed exception.
findings.fix_now: Do not change code (read-only lens). Flag MB-FOCUS-0035 as a HARD BLOCKER for whichever slice mounts FocusTracerStateHolder — it must ship a single-instance guard (e.g. an in-process mutex keyed by userId, or a liveness lease record checked before the drain) in the SAME change that adds the first production call-site, not as follow-up debt.
findings.definitive_fix: Add a liveness/lease token (owning process+holder id, monotonic-timestamped) written alongside the descriptor; `start()`'s drain only discards a scanned session whose lease is stale (no live holder claims it), never a session with a fresh lease. Additionally, checkpoint() should verify the descriptor it is pairing against still exists (or the store should reject an orphaned-snapshot write) so a destroyed write-ahead pair surfaces as `checkpointLost=true` instead of silently succeeding. Owning phase: the slice that first wires FocusTracerStateHolder to a screen (post-S5, per CONTRACT_INERT status).
findings.closing_test: A concurrency test: construct two FocusTracerStateHolder instances for the same userId sharing one SecureFocusSessionStore backing; start() holder A, then start() holder B; assert holder A's NEXT checkpoint() call surfaces a detectable failure (not silent Stored) OR assert B's drain refuses to discard A's live session. Today's suite has no such test (grep of FocusTracerStateHolderTest.kt confirms only a `SessionScan.Failed` regression test at line 486-492, nothing for a live sibling or a mid-drain discard failure).
findings.residual_risk: Even with a lease, a lease can itself go stale across a true crash (no clean release) — the fix must define a lease TTL and accept that a very recently-crashed holder's session may be legitimately drained by a next launch; that reintroduces (bounded) the same class of loss this finding describes, just narrowed to the crash-recovery window instead of live-concurrency window.

findings.title: The pre-session drain discards prior sessions' write-ahead records without consuming the typed FocusWriteOutcome result — contradicts this exact file's own stated purge-outcome discipline two methods later
findings.evidence: FocusTracerStateHolder.kt:154-157: `val scan = store.scanSessionIds(userId); if (scan is SessionScan.Scanned) { scan.sessionIds.forEach { id -> store.discard(userId, id) } }` — `store.discard(...)` returns `FocusWriteOutcome` (SecureFocusSessionStore.kt:169-174, a sealed Stored/Failed type specifically designed per its KDoc so a caller cannot silently drop a failed purge) but the return value here is discarded inside a bare `forEach`. Contrast with `complete()` at line 264 (`bufferPurged = store.discard(...) is FocusWriteOutcome.Stored`) and the class's own top-of-file KDoc item 4 (lines 47-49): 'PURGE ON COMPLETION, with its outcome consumed... a purge whose failure nobody reads is retention with a comment claiming otherwise.' The drain purge is the SAME kind of purge and violates the SAME principle stated three paragraphs above it in the same file.
findings.failure_mode: If an individual `store.discard(userId, id)` inside the drain fails (transient backend fault on either the snapshot or descriptor remove — SecureKeyValueStore is not guaranteed infallible per its own KDoc catch-blocks in SecureFocusSessionStore.kt:106-123), the orphaned encrypted descriptor+snapshot pair is left on disk with no counter, telemetry, or retry signal — silent indefinite retention of a stale (possibly PracticeOnly, possibly Measuring-but-abandoned) session's write-ahead data, discovered only by a future scan re-attempting (self-healing only if the fault was transient) or never.
findings.fix_now: None applied (read-only). Note for owning phase: wrap the drain in the same outcome-consuming pattern as `complete()`/`abandon()` — accumulate discard failures and surface them (breadcrumb/telemetry, not a crash) so a persistent per-key failure is at least observable.
findings.definitive_fix: `start()` should return or log a typed drain-outcome (e.g. `drainedCount`/`drainFailures: Set<String>`) so a caller/telemetry layer can detect accumulating orphans, matching the store's own `SessionScan.Failed` fail-visible pattern used one line above for the scan itself.
findings.closing_test: Unit test: inject a backing store whose `discard()` fails for one specific scanned sessionId (Failed) while others succeed; assert the failure is observable (not just that start() still returns Measuring) — no such test exists today (confirmed: only `a_start_whose_scan_cannot_read_the_index_still_seals_and_does_not_crash` covers the SCAN failing, none cover an individual DISCARD failing).
findings.residual_risk: Low standalone severity (encrypted-at-rest orphan accumulation, not a correctness bug for the CURRENT session) — but it compounds LENS4-01: an orphan left behind by a failed drain is indistinguishable, at the next scan, from a legitimately-abandoned session, and gets re-attempted forever without bound or backoff.

But AppGraph.kt:159 wires MindBoostStorageNamespaces.Focus2 into the PLAIN `accountBoundStores` map (blanket `clearNamespace()` path, AccountDeletionCoordinator.kt:67-69), NOT as a third `subjectScoped*Store` alongside `subjectScopedRunsStore`/`subjectScopedSessionsStore` (AccountDeletionCoordinator.kt:39-58). Separately, repo-wide grep for `SubjectRevocationAuthority|guardedWrite|guardedRead` across shared/src/commonMain/.../mindboost returns exactly 5 files, NONE of them in focus2/ — SecureFocusSessionStore.sealDescriptor/checkpoint/discard have no revocation-tombstone check before writing, unlike SecureSessionRecordStore/SecureCognitiveSessionRunStore which are guarded per the 2026-07-14 fix specifically to close this class of gap.
findings.failure_mode: Two distinct exposures, both structural: (a) on a device where a SECOND locally-authenticated account previously used Focus2 (sign-out doesn't purge local storage per AccountDeletionCoordinator.kt:30-31's own documented invariant), deleting the FIRST account's data blanket-clears `mindboost_focus2` and collaterally destroys the second account's own in-progress/completed-but-unpurged Focus2 sessions — the same collateral-wipe class the KDoc at lines 26-38 calls 'documented decision 2026-06-29, deferred', but never explicitly re-evaluated for the NEW Focus2 namespace at the time it was introduced. (b) unlike Sessions/SessionRuns, a stale/lagging Focus2 writer (e.g. a `checkpoint()` call already in flight, or a coroutine on a scope not torn down by sign-out — AccountDeletionCoordinator.kt has no scope-cancellation of concurrently-running feature coroutines, confirmed by grep for cancel/Job patterns returning zero matches) racing AFTER this SAME account's own erasure has completed is not blocked or detected at all — no tombstone check exists to refuse the write, so a completed erasure could be silently un-erased by its own trailing writer (the exact scenario SubjectRevocationAuthority was built to close for the other two stores).
findings.fix_now: None applied (read-only). Flag as pre-wiring blocker alongside LENS4-01.
findings.definitive_fix: Either (i) add Focus2 as a THIRD `subjectScoped*Store` in SecureNamespaceUserDataEraser/AccountDeletionCoordinator wired against the SAME shared `revocationStore` (mindboost_revocation), erased via a subject-scoped `deleteAll()` instead of blanket clearNamespace, and gate SecureFocusSessionStore's write methods through `SubjectRevocationAuthority.guardedWrite` the same way SecureSessionRecordStore does; or (ii) explicitly re-document why Focus2 is exempt from that treatment (e.g. if a product decision makes 'single Focus2 session in flight, ever' true by construction) — the current state is silent, not a documented exemption.
findings.closing_test: (a) Erasure isolation test: two userIds share one Focus2 backing store; erase user A; assert user B's Focus2 rows survive (mirrors AccountBoundErasureCoverageTest / the Sessions/SessionRuns isolation tests). (b) Anti-resurrection test: mark user A revoked via SubjectRevocationAuthority/revocationStore, then attempt `SecureFocusSessionStore.checkpoint(userA, ...)`; assert it is refused, not silently Stored. Neither test exists today for focus2 (grep of SecureFocusSessionStoreTest.kt shows no revocation-related test names).
findings.residual_risk: Since focus2 is CONTRACT_INERT (no production writer), exploitability today is zero; this is purely a pre-wiring architectural gap. If the eventual wiring decision is genuinely 'one measurement session ever, synchronous, no backgrounding' the risk may be acceptable by design — but that decision has not been stated anywhere I found (grep of ADR_FOCUS_TEMPORAL_QUALITY.md / CURRENT_AUTHORITY_INDEX.md was not exhaustive on this specific point).

findings.title: FocusSessionState.toGlobalStatus() — the documented bridge from focus2's local lifecycle to the repo's global SessionStatus/recovery-scan machinery — has zero production call-sites; focus2 built a second, fully parallel, non-integrated write-ahead+recovery system instead of plugging into the ratified one
findings.evidence: FocusSessionLifecycle.kt:126-140 defines `fun FocusSessionState.toGlobalStatus(): SessionStatus?` with KDoc 'Maps the local runtime state onto the GLOBAL lifecycle record, at write-ahead points only.' Repo-wide grep for `toGlobalStatus|FocusSessionLifecycle` (as a symbol reference) returns exactly one production definition site plus one desktopTest file (FocusSessionLifecycleTest.kt) that calls the mapping function directly in isolation — no call in FocusTracerStateHolder.kt, SecureFocusSessionStore.kt, or anywhere else in commonMain that would actually write a `SecureSessionRecordStore`/`mindboost_sessions` row from a focus2 lifecycle transition.
findings.failure_mode: focus2 sessions will never register with the global session-lifecycle/recovery-scan infrastructure (`SecureSessionRecordStore`, whatever 'abandoned session' recovery/analytics other MindBoost modules rely on) that this same repo already ratified and reuses across other slices (per project memory: SYSTEM-1 CognitiveSessionRun's 'reuso total' principle explicitly reuses SessionRecord/SyncQueue/RecoveryScanner). The mapping function exists and is unit-pinned but is decorative until wired — a reviewer skimming for 'is global lifecycle integration done' would find a plausible-looking, tested function and reasonably (but incorrectly) conclude yes.
findings.fix_now: None applied (read-only).
findings.definitive_fix: Wire `toGlobalStatus()` into FocusTracerStateHolder's write-ahead points (start/pause/complete/abandon) against an injected SecureSessionRecordStore, OR explicitly document that Focus2 intentionally does NOT participate in the global recovery scan and explain the product/architecture reason (e.g. it has its own richer restore via FocusSessionRestore and double-registering would be redundant) — either is fine, but the current silent gap is not a decision, it's an omission.
findings.closing_test: Integration test asserting that a FocusTracerStateHolder.start() call results in a SessionStatus.STARTED row visible via SecureSessionRecordStore for that user — does not exist today.
findings.residual_risk: Low direct harm (focus2's OWN restore path, FocusSessionRestore.kt, is independently sound and fail-closed) — the risk is purely at the product/ops layer: whatever cross-module 'you have N abandoned sessions, resume?' surface exists today silently excludes Focus2, and nobody auditing that surface would know to look here.

findings.fix_now: None — nothing to fix, nothing exists.

lenses.lens: LENS 5 — privacy/security/data-lifecycle (§3.7), MindBoost Focus V5 · S5 · R3 · Paso 7, HEAD 8a06b9acdfb93c83b9d8d4508c3c10ca8dc0f3e5
lenses.verdict: FAIL (ceiling: DATA_LIFECYCLE_UNVERIFIED / BLOCKED_FOR_WIRING). Per-field flow for the summary-tier data (FocusRuntimeSnapshot tallies, FocusSessionDescriptor) is genuinely minimized and matches the ADR's own claims (VERIFIED_PRIMARY: no per-trial raw, no ordered series, payload-free telemetry, no export surface). But the account-deletion/revocation guarantee for the NEW `mindboost_focus2` namespace is unverified end-to-end: GAP-1 (live TOCTOU resurrection past account deletion) and GAP-2 (cross-account collateral wipe) are real, self-documented by the ADR (R3-12) and CONFIRMED here against the actual code, with ZERO regression test — unlike the sibling Sessions/SessionRuns stores that already have dedicated revocation-gap suites. The prior handoff's 'security APTO' (S5_R3_P7_HANDOFF.md:76) is NOT defensible as an unconditional pass: the underlying lens record is verifiably absent from the repo (DOCUMENTATION_SECURITY_REVIEW_ONLY at best, and not even that — the documentation itself is missing), and the same CRITICAL gap was caught by a DIFFERENT ('privacy') lens in the SAME handoff. Practical exploitability today is zero only because focus2 is CONTRACT_INERT (unwired); the failure mode is that 'security APTO' could be cited later to green-light wiring without closing GAP-1/GAP-2 first.

findings.title: GAP-1 (revocation not wired into focus2 write-ahead store) is real AND has zero regression test, unlike its own sibling stores
findings.evidence: shared/.../focus2/data/session/SecureFocusSessionStore.kt:106-123 — write()/remove() call `store.put`/`store.remove` directly, no SubjectRevocationAuthority/guardedWrite/guardedRead anywhere in the file (grep for Revocation|guardedRead|guardedWrite in the whole focus2/ tree = 1 hit, an unrelated KDoc sentence about the consent record's own `revoke()`). `FocusWriteOutcome` (lines 169-174) is `Stored|Failed` only — no `RejectedRevoked` variant exists to even express a revocation rejection. Contrast: `SecureSessionRecordStore.kt:100,205` and `SecureCognitiveSessionRunStore.kt:92,152` both construct `SubjectRevocationAuthority(revocationStore)` and call `markRevoked`/guard reads, and BOTH have dedicated red-team suites (`SessionRecordStoreRevocationGapsTest.kt`, `CognitiveSessionRunStoreRevocationGapsTest.kt`). Glob of `shared/src/desktopTest/.../focus2/**` (25 files) contains no `*RevocationGaps*` file and no cross-account test for `SecureFocusSessionStoreTest.kt`.
findings.failure_mode: If/when focus2 is wired (the point of this whole slice), a write-ahead `checkpoint()` for a subject mid-deletion can race the blanket `clearNamespace()` and land AFTER erasure completes, durably re-persisting cognitive session data for an account that reported 'deleted' — a GDPR Art. 17 violation that reproduces the exact class of bug already found and fixed for Sessions/SessionRuns in slice 6-R3, now reintroduced in brand-new code with no test to catch a regression or prove a future fix.
findings.fix_now: Do not treat GAP-1 as closed by prose. Before any `focus2Enabled` wiring: land a `SecureFocusSessionStoreRevocationGapsTest` (mirror the two existing sibling suites) that marks a subject revoked via `SubjectRevocationAuthority` and asserts `sealDescriptor`/`checkpoint` reject rather than write.
findings.definitive_fix: Implement the ADR's own contract verbatim (ADR_FOCUS_TEMPORAL_QUALITY.md:307-326): inject `SubjectRevocationAuthority` into `SecureFocusSessionStore`/`SecureFocusConsentStore`, add `FocusWriteOutcome.RejectedRevoked`, route all writes through `guardedWrite`, reads through triadic `guardedRead`, and move Focus2 out of the blanket-clear list into the subject-scoped erase path (same as Sessions/SessionRuns) in `AppGraph.kt`. Owning phase: must land before/with the wiring slice that sets `focus2Enabled = true`.
findings.closing_test: A red-team suite proving: (a) a write attempted after `markRevoked(subject)` returns `RejectedRevoked` and leaves no key in the backing store (deterministic race via `GatedSecureKeyValueStore`+`CompletableDeferred`, not sleeps, per the ADR's own prescription at line 325); (b) a new dedicated test asserts Focus2 uses the subject-scoped erase path, not blanket clear.
findings.residual_risk: Static/structural evidence only — I did not dynamically reproduce the race under test execution (READ-ONLY constraint).

findings.title: "security APTO" (S5_R3_P7_HANDOFF.md:76) has no recoverable primary record and is contradicted by the SAME handoff's privacy lens in the SAME review — not defensible as an unconditional pass
findings.evidence: S5_R3_P7_HANDOFF.md:36-38 states the lens tracker `scratchpad/S5_R3_lens_integration.md` is NOT preserved in this tree ('efímero') and that on this basis Paso 7 itself refuses to declare '7/7 APTO' as a fact. I independently confirmed the file is absent: `find . -iname "S5_R3_lens_integration*"` over the whole repo returns zero hits. Yet line 76-77 still reports a per-lens table with 'security APTO' unconditional, while 'privacy APTO_CON_OBSERVACIONES' (same document, line 76, and line 82-83: P1 'subject-revocation focus2 = PENDING (MB-FOCUS-0048)') flags the exact GAP-1/GAP-2 issue as an open item under a DIFFERENT lens label. No `agent_outputs/` file for this R3 P7 reaudit's 'security' lens exists (the only `04_privacy_security.md` in that directory is from an earlier S1-era slice, combines both concerns, and does not discuss GAP-1/GAP-2 at all — grep for DPIA/GDPR/health in it returns only one unrelated retention-policy line).
findings.failure_mode: A downstream reader (CEO, next auditor, or an orchestrating agent) sees 'security APTO' as an unconditional pass and could use it to justify wiring focus2 or skipping a security re-review, while the actual security-relevant defect (unauthorized data resurrection past a revocation boundary — an access-control bug, not merely a retention nicety) sits unresolved one line away under a differently-labeled lens whose primary evidence is also gone. This is precisely 'falsely promotes an unvalidated system toward launch.'
findings.fix_now: Downgrade 'security APTO' in any forward-facing summary to 'UNVERIFIABLE / NOT_DEFENSIBLE (primary record absent)' until re-run with a checked-in artifact.
findings.definitive_fix: Require every lens verdict in a Paso-7-style multi-lens gate to be backed by a checked-in (not scratchpad) artifact stating scope, checklist, and evidence citations — mirror the durable `agent_outputs/NN_lens.md` pattern already used elsewhere in this same docs tree — before the verdict is quoted in a handoff. Re-run the security lens with GAP-1/GAP-2 explicitly in its checklist (they are squarely an authorization/TOCTOU defect, core AppSec scope, not solely 'privacy').
findings.residual_risk: Even after this, whatever the original 'security' lens actually inspected (scope, tooling, depth) is unrecoverable — this finding cannot be fully closed retroactively, only prevented going forward.
findings.closing_test: A `validate-authority-entrypoints.mjs`-style script (the repo already has this pattern) that fails the build/handoff generation if a lens verdict is asserted without a corresponding checked-in `agent_outputs/` (or equivalent) file for that specific review round.

findings.title: GAP-2 cross-account collateral wipe: Focus2 is NEW code that reintroduces a pattern already identified and fixed for Sessions/SessionRuns in the same repo
findings.evidence: `SecureFocusSessionStore.kt:149-152` keys are subject-scoped BY CONVENTION (`focus2_session:$userId:...`), the identical pattern `AccountDeletionCoordinator.kt:34` calls out (`run:<uid>::<sid>`) as needing the subject-scoped fix. But `AppGraph.kt:148-182` wires `focus2Store` only into the plain `accountBoundStores` map (line 159) and never passes it as `subjectScopedRunsStore`/`subjectScopedSessionsStore` (lines 184-190 only cover Sessions/SessionRuns). `AccountDeletionCoordinator.kt:67-69` therefore runs `store.clearNamespace()` (a FULL namespace wipe) over `focus2Store` on any account deletion.
findings.failure_mode: On a device with two locally-authenticated accounts (the KDoc at `AccountDeletionCoordinator.kt:26-37` explicitly documents sign-out never purges local storage, so this scenario is reachable), deleting account A will delete account B's in-flight/unsynced focus2 session buffer and consent record too, even though B never asked for anything to be erased.
findings.fix_now: Same as L5-01's definitive fix — they share one implementation.
findings.definitive_fix: As in L5-01 (move Focus2 to the subject-scoped erase path in AppGraph).
findings.closing_test: A test mirroring `SecureNamespaceUserDataEraserSessionsTest.kt`: seed `focus2_session:alice:*` and `focus2_session:bob:*` keys in the same backing store, erase alice, assert bob's keys survive.

findings.title: The TRIAL_JOURNAL consent gate (FocusJournalAdmission) has zero production call-sites — the exact 'control with no call-site is cover, not protection' anti-pattern its own KDoc warns against for the scope it just deleted
findings.evidence: `FocusDataConsent.kt:26-29` explicitly documents removing a prior `RESEARCH` scope 'because nothing consumed it — FocusJournalAdmission structurally denies research purposes, so the scope enforced exactly nothing... A control with no call-site is cover, not protection.' `grep -r FocusJournalAdmission shared/src/commonMain/.../focus2` returns only `FocusJournalAdmission.kt` itself and this one KDoc mention — no actual invocation from any runtime/session-store call-site. The per-trial journal writer described in ADR-FOCUS-DATA 'does not yet exist' (SecureFocusSessionStore.kt KDoc), so today this is inert, not exploitable.
findings.failure_mode: The pattern is currently harmless only because nothing writes a journal yet. If a future change adds the journal writer directly against SecureFocusSessionStore (the natural place, since it already owns write-ahead persistence) without routing it through FocusJournalAdmission/FocusConsentStore, over-collection would ship with the consent-gate code present but silently bypassed — indistinguishable from 'we checked consent' in a diff review.
findings.fix_now: None required today (inert). Document explicitly in the ADR that FocusJournalAdmission currently has zero callers so future reviewers don't mistake its existence for enforcement.
findings.definitive_fix: When the journal writer is built (S6+), make the consent check structurally unavoidable — the journal-writing function should take a ScopedConsent/JournalAdmission value as a required, non-defaultable parameter obtained ONLY from FocusConsentStore.status(...), so a call-site cannot compile without going through the gate.
findings.closing_test: Once the journal writer exists: a test asserting the writer function has no overload/path that skips FocusJournalAdmission, plus a red-team test that an unconsented (UNKNOWN/REVOKED/UNAVAILABLE) subject's journal write is refused.

findings.title: DPIA for disability-proxy signals (screenReaderActive / switchAccessActive / SWITCH_SEQUENTIAL modality) is self-classified as GDPR-sensitive ('afín a discapacidad') but only a forward TODO, never a completed artifact
findings.evidence: ADR_FOCUS_TEMPORAL_QUALITY.md:415,426 — 'DPIA (proxies de tecnología asistiva)' is listed as finding F-R3-J, gated on 'S6 acceptance gate + copy-scanner', and line 426 says explicitly 'asistiva (afín a discapacidad), ya minimizados; documentar en DPIA' (document in a DPIA — future tense). No DPIA document exists under docs/ for this (grep for DPIA across docs/engines/focus_v5 returns only forward-looking mentions, never a completed assessment). FocusSessionDescriptor.kt:62,252-284 (screenReaderActive, AccessibilityContext.switchAccessActive) confirms these fields ARE captured and sealed into the persisted, account-bound, encrypted descriptor once a session runs.
findings.failure_mode: Assistive-technology usage is a recognized proxy for disability status (special-category-adjacent under GDPR Art. 9 in several interpretations). Shipping collection of this signal with only a forward-declared DPIA, gated on an S6 milestone that has not happened, means the actual legal risk assessment could be skipped if S6 is compressed or the gate is treated as a checkbox rather than a real review.
findings.fix_now: Nothing to code today (data is not yet flowing — CONTRACT_INERT). Flag this explicitly as a go/no-go blocker in the S6 acceptance criteria rather than a soft TODO.
findings.definitive_fix: Produce and check in an actual DPIA covering screenReaderActive/switchAccessActive/inputModality before focus2Enabled is set to true in any build users receive; the S6 gate should require the artifact to exist, not merely be 'planned'.
findings.closing_test: A checklist/scanner gate (mirroring mindboostCopySafetyScanner's build-time enforcement style) that fails if focus2Enabled (once it exists) is flipped without a corresponding DPIA document reference in the ADR register.

findings.title: No minors/age-based escalation mechanism exists anywhere in the app for cognitive/behavioral or disability-proxy data collection (product-wide gap, not focus2-specific)
findings.evidence: Repo-wide grep (shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/com/mindos/app, case-insensitive) for minor|parental|age.?gate|edad_minima returns no genuine hits (11 files matched only on unrelated substrings, e.g. arena/matchmaking enums). No age-gate, parental-consent flow, or minimum-age check was found anywhere in the app.

findings.fix_now: None specific to this slice — out of scope for focus2 alone; belongs to a product-level privacy decision.
findings.definitive_fix: A product-level decision (owner: privacy/legal, not this engineering slice) on whether the app is marketed/available to minors, and if so, an age-gate + parental-consent flow before any behavioral or accessibility-signal capture is enabled broadly.
findings.closing_test: N/A at this slice's scope; track as a separate product/privacy work item.
findings.residual_risk: Grep-based absence claims cannot rule out naming conventions I did not anticipate; treat as a strong signal, not proof of total absence.

lenses.limitations: READ-ONLY, no build/test execution — all "confirmed absent" claims (no revocation-gap test for focus2, no lens-tracker artifact, no minors mechanism) are grep/find-based and could in principle miss a differently-named file; I did not run the desktopTest suite so I cannot independently confirm the existing green baseline holds on this exact tree, nor dynamically exercise the actual runtime race in L5-01/L5-03 (only static/code-structural evidence — GAP-1/GAP-2 are STATICALLY/VERIFIED_PRIMARY as absent-of-guard from direct source reads, not dynamically reproduced by me; the ADR's own R3-12 section already asserts them as "vivo" from its own prior analysis, which I independently corroborated against the real file contents rather than trusting the prose). findings.title: Entire R3 authority chain is UNTRACKED — absent from HEAD 8a06b9ac that every header claims as provenance; not reproducible from git

findings.title: Review class mislabeled EXTERNAL_AUDIT / 'auditoría de ChatGPT' on every authoritative surface and baked into the ADR state token, while the producer's own tooling says AI_ASSISTED_INDEPENDENT_REVIEW
findings.evidence: Authoritative surface says EXTERNAL: S5_R3_P7_HANDOFF.md L1/L4 ('entrega a auditoría externa', 'auditoría de ChatGPT') L6/L38 ('La aprobación la da esta auditoría externa'); CURRENT_AUTHORITY_INDEX.md L22/L24; ADR_REGISTER_V5.md L26 status token `REOPENED_AFTER_EXTERNAL_AUDIT`; S5_R3_EVIDENCE_CAPSULE.md L32; MINDBOOST_AUDIT_LEDGER.md L22/L259/L374/L427 ('returned CANDIDATA to external audit (the authority that approves)'). The producer's OWN tools say the opposite: build_external_manifest.mjs L71/L97 `AI_ASSISTED_INDEPENDENT_REVIEW (not a human/institutional EXTERNAL_AUDIT)`; reaudit/S5_R3_REAUDIT_COMMAND_LOG.md L54 'Human/institutional external audit: NOT_OBTAINED (this is AI_ASSISTED_INDEPENDENT_REVIEW)'.
findings.failure_mode: The gate that promotes ADR-FOCUS-TEMPORAL-QUALITY from R2→R3 (and the reopening token itself) is attributed to an 'external audit,' when it is another LLM chat. A CEO reading `REOPENED_AFTER_EXTERNAL_AUDIT · pendiente de aprobación de auditoría externa` reasonably believes independent human/institutional scrutiny gates the ADR; the actual gate is an AI review. This inflates the assurance class of the sign-off and mis-attributes audit authority — a governance-integrity defect, self-contradicted by the producer's own manifest/command-log.
findings.fix_now: Replace EXTERNAL_AUDIT / 'auditoría externa' / 'auditoría de ChatGPT' with AI_ASSISTED_INDEPENDENT_REVIEW across handoff/index/register/capsule/ledger, rename the ADR token to `REOPENED_AFTER_AI_ASSISTED_REVIEW`, and state 'human/institutional external audit = NOT_OBTAINED.'

findings.residual_risk: None; correction is honest downgrade of assurance claim.

findings.title: Package closure not achieved and defined twice with conflicting rules; the authoritative handoff excludes the harness and the real scorer
findings.evidence: Two package definitions disagree. (1) Authoritative handoff §6 INCLUDE list (S5_R3_P7_HANDOFF.md L94-95) lists docs+scanner+ledger+ADR but NOT r2_falsification_harness.mjs and NOT focus2/domain/scoring/DescriptiveScorer.kt; ships truncated 16-hex; ledger hash out-of-band. (2) reaudit/build_external_manifest.mjs (untracked, never referenced by the handoff) has the correct rules (full 64-hex+bytes+EOL+last-byte, ledger+harness included) BUT its MEMBERS list references 4 files that do not exist — S5_R3_REAUDIT_MASTER_REPORT.md, S5_R3_REAUDIT_FINDINGS.json, S5_R3_MULTIDIMENSIONAL_VERDICTS.md, S5_R3_DATAFLOW_THREATMODEL.md (verified MISSING) — and its own outputs S5_R3_EXTERNAL_MANIFEST.json/.md were never emitted (MISSING).
findings.failure_mode: R2 arithmetic is reproducible from the capsule's embedded formula + a probit, but the package alone cannot confirm that formula EQUALS the compiled scorer, because DescriptiveScorer.kt is excluded from the shipped set; and no closed manifest exists to bind the members. The only closure tool points at 4 phantom members and produced no output, so 'package closure' is aspirational, not realized. An auditor receives an incomplete, internally contradictory package.
findings.fix_now: Adopt build_external_manifest.mjs as the single package definition, add DescriptiveScorer.kt+Probit.kt (or a byte-pinned excerpt) and the harness to MEMBERS, drop or create the 4 phantom members, run the builder, and commit its emitted S5_R3_EXTERNAL_MANIFEST.json/.md.

findings.evidence: scripts/validate-authority-entrypoints.mjs: check (1) L36-40 greps 2 hardcoded entrypoints for one marker via substring `includes()` (a quoted/commented mention passes — weaker than its own L46 declaration classifier); check (2) L46-50 forbids >1 `AUTHORITY_INDEX_ROLE: CURRENT` line within focus_v5/*.md; check (3) L53-58 forbids only 2 hardcoded legacy files (FOCUS_ENGINE_MASTER_PLAN_V5.md, GATE_CATALOG_V5.md) from carrying the index marker/role. It enforces none of that — only that a marker string is present in 2 files and that a specific role line is unique. findings.title: 'VERIFIED_PRIMARY … reproduced with the real scorer' rounds up the evidence class: the falsification was reproduced by a Node transcription of the formula, not by executing DescriptiveScorer.kt

lenses.lens: LENS 7 — accessibility / equity / UX / safety (§3.8): access-to-training vs measurement-comparability in focus2 presentation (screen-reader/switch/Dynamic-Type/reduced-motion), differential missingness, honest "not measured" state, RT-as-feedback.
lenses.verdict: FAIL (ceiling: focus2's §3.8 accessibility/equity posture is NOT launch-blessable). The RT lane and the "never withhold training" half are handled well (RT is never shown as feedback; the exercise always runs; typed absence states with no fabricated zeros). But the ACCURACY lane — the primary construct (d'/criterion) — pools assistive-tech sessions whose accessible rendering is NOT construct-equivalent, under an explicit-but-false "accuracy is modality-fair" premise. Because focus2 is CONTRACT_INERT (not wired), every finding is latent, not a live harm; they become live/mis-attributing the moment the tracer is mounted. All findings are design/static-verified, not runtime-observed.

findings.title: Screen-reader contentDescription announces the correct answer AND the congruency condition; the accuracy lane never gates screenReaderActive, so a screen-reader user's fabricated-high accuracy pools as PROVISIONAL evidence
findings.evidence: FocusTracerScreen.kt:136-138 contentDescription = "El elemento central apunta a la $direction. Los elementos que lo rodean son $side." with direction = izquierda/derecha (line 136) and side = if(congruent) "iguales" else "distintos" (line 129). VectorFilterModel.kt:106 correctResponse = if(centrePointsLeft) LEFT else RIGHT, i.e. direction 'izquierda' IS the correct answer. FocusEvidenceStatePolicy.kt:42-48 evidenceOf() gates on writeAhead/dose/scorerInvalidated/temporal backstop only — NO screenReaderActive term — with a comment (lines 30-32) asserting 'accuracy is modality-fair (charter §14)'. FocusSessionDescriptor.rtEvidenceAdmissible (line 151) excludes screen-reader RT but there is no accuracyEvidenceAdmissible sibling.
findings.failure_mode: For VoiceOver/TalkBack, the flanker's accessible label states the correct response verbatim ('apunta a la izquierda') and verbalizes the entire experimental manipulation ('iguales'/'distintos'), collapsing the visual-interference construct to zero. A screen-reader user taps what they heard: accuracy ~100%, d' fabricated-high, criterion meaningless. StimulusRow's own KDoc (lines 118-124) claims 'the accessible version has to remain the same exercise, or its results mean something else' — the mitigation (one label instead of eleven arrows) achieved the opposite by handing over the answer. Once wired, this mis-attributes inflated attention/filtering evidence to a protected group.
findings.fix_now: Make screen-reader sessions accuracy-inadmissible, symmetric with rtEvidenceAdmissible: add descriptor.accuracyEvidenceAdmissible = !screenReaderActive and gate FocusEvidenceStatePolicy.evidenceOf() on it (screen-reader ⇒ TRAINING_ONLY, still fully playable). Separately, stop the label from naming the answer/condition: describe the raw stimulus geometry ('flecha central; 4 flechas alrededor'), never the derived direction or the congruency word.
findings.closing_test: Property test: for every trial, StimulusRow's contentDescription must NOT contain the correctResponse's direction word nor the congruency label ('iguales'/'distintos'). Policy test: evidenceOf(screenReaderActive=true, all-else-admissible) == TRAINING_ONLY, with a discriminating half where screenReaderActive=false ⇒ PROVISIONAL.
findings.definitive_fix: S5/Paso-7 must decide whether the flanker is a valid construct under a screen reader at all; if not, screen-reader sessions are training-only for BOTH lanes and a non-visual attention construct is a separate exercise with its own ADR. Owning phase: S5 evidence-state wiring + a Cognitive-Science sign-off on construct equivalence.
findings.residual_risk: Even with the label neutralized, a linearized audio flanker may not engage spatial visual filtering; 'same exercise for screen-reader users' may be unachievable and should be stated as a limitation, not engineered around.

findings.title: 'Accuracy is modality-fair' is false for sequential/switch input: a single fixed response window (1200 ms, not modality-adjusted) must absorb TWO switch activations, so switch users' accuracy is depressed by timeouts and still pools
findings.evidence: FocusTracerStateHolder.kt:129 withTimeoutOrNull(run.descriptor.spec.responseWindowMs) — one window for all modalities, from the sealed spec. VectorFilterSpec.DEFAULT_RESPONSE_WINDOW_MS = 1200 (VectorFilterModel.kt:66). SequentialResponses (FocusTracerScreen.kt:204-215) requires onAdvanceCursor THEN onActivateCursor (up to two taps) to answer, vs one tap for TouchResponses. Expired window ⇒ Response.NONE ⇒ a miss (FocusRuntimeModel.kt:254-255). FocusEvidenceStatePolicy.kt:30-32 explicitly excludes modality from the SESSION (accuracy) lane; only rtShadowAdmissible gates it (lines 51-57).
findings.failure_mode: A switch/sequential user (and any user mis-routed to that UI, see L7-03) must complete two activations inside a window designed for one touch. Missed deadlines become Response.NONE misses, deflating hit rate and d'. That deflated accuracy pools into PROVISIONAL evidence because the accuracy lane is modality-blind. This is both an access-to-completion barrier (the exercise may be un-finishable in time via switches) and a measurement confound (attention estimate contaminated by input-path speed) — the mirror image of L7-01's inflation.
findings.fix_now: Either (a) extend the response window as a function of modality (and record the extension in the descriptor so it is auditable), or (b) mark sequential-modality sessions accuracy-inadmissible (TRAINING_ONLY) exactly as proposed for screen readers, since the current pooling under a modality-blind accuracy lane is unsound in either direction.
findings.closing_test: Simulation test: an honest sequential responder whose per-activation cost forces >window on N% of trials produces depressed hit-rate; assert the resulting session is NOT PROVISIONAL (either extended-window keeps it fair, or it lands TRAINING_ONLY). Discriminating half: same responder under TOUCH_DIRECT stays PROVISIONAL.
findings.definitive_fix: Define a modality-specific timing contract (window derived from measured switch-scan cadence) OR a portfolio rule that sequential accuracy is a distinct comparison class, never pooled with touch accuracy. Owning phase: S5 timing/eligibility + portfolio comparability rules.
findings.residual_risk: A modality-extended window changes the temporal construct too; may cascade into the temporal-quality gate. Needs joint design, not a local constant bump.

findings.title: Android modality selection is a self-admitted heuristic that is the ONLY selector (declaration UI absent); common non-AT accessibility services false-positive able-bodied users into the SWITCH_SEQUENTIAL UI and modality class with no user override
findings.evidence: FocusAccessibility.android.kt:38-48 read(): switchAccessActive = manager.isEnabled && getEnabledAccessibilityServiceList(FEEDBACK_ALL_MASK).isNotEmpty() && !screenReader — the KDoc (lines 22-30) admits false positives (autofill, screen filter) and false negatives (external switch/keyboard/head-pointer) and calls the manual choice a 'DECLARED GAP ... does not exist yet'. AccessibilityContext.directTouchDeclared 'is false everywhere today' (FocusSessionDescriptor.kt:253-260); impliedModality therefore never returns TOUCH_DIRECT (lines 273-278). FocusRunPlanner.kt:93 seals inputModality = accessibility.impliedModality; FocusTracerScreen.kt:103-106 renders SequentialResponses whenever modality == SWITCH_SEQUENTIAL.
findings.failure_mode: Any user with an enabled accessibility service that is not touch-exploration (password managers, clipboard tools, Tasker, screen dimmers, many OEM services — extremely common on Android) is silently switched to the multi-step focus-ring input UI they do not need and cannot opt out of, and the session is sealed as SWITCH_SEQUENTIAL. That is (a) a confusing/slower UX imposed on the wrong users, (b) a measurement mislabel that (per L7-02) can deflate their accuracy, and (c) differential by device configuration/age/OEM. Symmetrically, real external-switch users are false-negatived into a touch-only UI. Detection being the sole selector is exactly the structural inequity REDTEAM #34 names, shipped as the default.
findings.fix_now: Do not mount the tracer until the pre-seal manual modality choice exists (the code's own declared correct answer). Interim: never DERIVE modality from the heuristic alone — treat undetermined as UNKNOWN and offer an explicit in-flow toggle before the seal; the heuristic may only pre-select, never lock.
findings.closing_test: Test that a non-touch-exploration a11y service does NOT by itself force InputModality.SWITCH_SEQUENTIAL without an explicit participant declaration; and that a declared touch user seals TOUCH_DIRECT regardless of enabled services.
findings.definitive_fix: Ship the pre-seal modality declaration UI (MB-FOCUS declared gap) as a hard precondition of mounting; make impliedModality advisory only. Owning phase: the slice that mounts the tracer (currently unbuilt; S3 KDoc assigns single-instance/mount ownership to it).
findings.residual_risk: A declaration UI adds a pre-session step that some users skip/misanswer; needs a safe default (UNKNOWN ⇒ deny pooling) and must not gate access to training.

findings.title: No Dynamic-Type / font-scale capture or overflow-safe layout: large-font (low-vision, older) stimulus can overflow the fixed 160dp box and the unwrapped flanker Row; font scale is an uncaptured confound that pools into accuracy while screen-reader state is captured
findings.evidence: grep of focus2 for fontScale/LocalDensity/Dynamic-Type = 0 hits (no capture, no layout guard). Stimulus renders in a fixed Box(fillMaxWidth().height(160.dp)) (FocusTracerScreen.kt:92) with an unwrapped Row of displayLarge/displaySmall glyphs (lines 132-143). The descriptor captures screenReaderActive (FocusSessionDescriptor.kt:62) but has NO field for user font scale / display density. Accuracy lane pools regardless (FocusEvidenceStatePolicy.kt:42-48).
findings.failure_mode: A low-vision or older user relying on system font scaling (not TalkBack) enlarges glyphs; with flankerCount 4+ in an unwrapped Row and a 160dp-tall fixed box, large scales can clip/push flankers off-screen or truncate the stimulus vertically — altering the very stimulus whose interference is being measured. Because font scale is never captured, this stratum is invisible: their (possibly degraded) accuracy pools with everyone else's, a differential missingness by age/disability that the design's screen-reader capture does not cover.
findings.fix_now: Capture display font scale/density in the descriptor alongside screenReaderActive (so the stratum is at least visible/auditable). Make StimulusRow overflow-safe (constrain glyph size or allow the row to scroll/scale so no flanker is clipped) and pin it with a large-font layout test.
findings.closing_test: Compose layout test at fontScale 1.0/1.5/2.0: assert all flanker glyphs + centre are fully within bounds (no clip) for the maximum flankerCount. Descriptor test: font scale is a sealed field.
findings.definitive_fix: Decide (Cognitive-Science + UX) whether font-scale beyond a threshold changes the construct enough to mark the session accuracy-training-only, mirroring the screen-reader gate. Owning phase: S5 eligibility + on-device Accessibility Scanner / large-font verification.
findings.residual_risk: Overflow behavior is only provable on-device; JVM/desktop tests can pin measured widths but not the real Accessibility Scanner outcome.

findings.title: The a11y test suite proves geometry (size table) and the switch cursor model but NOT construct-preservation; reduced-motion is satisfied only by an unenforced 'no animation' convention with no hook/test for the S4 vigilance tracer
findings.evidence: FocusAccessibilityTest.kt asserts only ANDROID/IOS minimums differ (lines 24-33), desktop follows the larger (36-40), and cursor reachability/activation (44-75) — its own KDoc (lines 10-16) scopes it to 'the target-size TABLE and the switch-access INTERACTION MODEL', nothing about label validity. No test asserts the stimulus label does not leak the answer (see L7-01). grep of focus2 for animate/reducedMotion/Animatable = 0 hits; reduced-motion rests on the FocusTracerScreen KDoc convention 'No decorative animation' (lines 42-45) with no code hook. The S4 Sentinel/vigilance paradigm has domain files but NO screen yet (glob: no Sentinel*Screen).
findings.failure_mode: The accessibility tests are geometry theatre: they pass while the accessible rendering destroys construct validity (L7-01) and while large-font clipping (L7-04) goes unmeasured — giving the Paso-7 evidence capsule false comfort that §3.8 is covered. Reduced-motion is fine today only because nothing moves; when S4's jittered vigilance tracer lands (which the code repeatedly anticipates), there is no reduced-motion contract or test to stop decorative/temporal motion from being added as a confound.
findings.fix_now: Add the anti-leak label test and the large-font layout test from L7-01/L7-04 to this suite so 'accessibility passing' means construct-preserving, not just 48dp. Add a documented reduced-motion invariant (assert no infinite/decorative animation in the tracer) as an executable guard, not a comment.
findings.closing_test: The L7-01 label test and L7-04 layout test live here; plus a test that fails if any Animatable/rememberInfiniteTransition is introduced into the tracer screen without a reduced-motion branch.
findings.definitive_fix: S4 must define a reduced-motion contract for the vigilance tracer (functional motion only, honored under system reduce-motion) before its screen exists. Owning phase: S4 vigilance-tracer presentation.
findings.residual_risk: Executable 'no animation' guards are brittle; the real reduced-motion guarantee needs on-device verification with the system setting toggled.

lenses.limitations: WHAT I COULD NOT VERIFY: (1) Runtime/on-device behavior — READ-ONLY, no build/emulator; every finding is static/design (STATICALLY_VERIFIED or INFERENCE), and per the ground truth focus2 is CONTRACT_INERT (grep confirms no focus2Enabled/production call-site), so NONE are live harms today — they are latent-until-wired. exit-0/grep-miss ≠ behavior proof. (2) The user-facing framing of the honest 'not measured' state: FocusEvidenceState (TRAINING_ONLY/PROVISIONAL/INVALIDATED) and temporal NotCaptured appear only in domain + tests, and NO presentation/ui file renders them (grep) — so I confirmed the STATE MODEL is honest (typed absence, no fabricated zeros, OFFICIAL_ELIGIBLE inconstructible) but could NOT verify the eventual UI copy avoids user-blame; NOT_VERIFIABLE until a screen renders it.
